questions.topic: Current affairs – Regional, National and International
questions.subtopic: International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists 2026
questions.stem: For the United Nations' 2026 International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists (IYRP), which organisation was designated as the lead agency for the observance?
options: Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)
International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)
United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
explanations: Correct. The UN General Assembly declared 2026 the IYRP, and FAO is the lead agency coordinating the observance with partners.
UNEP works on environmental matters, but FAO was designated as the lead agency for IYRP 2026.
IFAD supports rural development and investment, but it is not the designated lead agency for this observance.
UNDP leads broader development work, but the IYRP lead-agency role belongs to FAO.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Current affairs – Regional, National and International; FAO, International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists 2026; UNGA Resolution A/RES/76/253; https://www.fao.org/rangelands-pastoralists-2026/about/

questions.topic: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology
questions.subtopic: Aditya-L1 halo orbit around Sun–Earth L1
questions.stem: Why is Aditya-L1 placed in a halo orbit around the Sun–Earth L1 point for its solar-observation mission?
options: It enables a continuous view of the Sun without occultation or eclipses by Earth.
It places the spacecraft inside Earth's atmosphere to sample auroras directly.
L1 is a point where all gravitational forces become zero, so the spacecraft can remain motionless.
It places the spacecraft between Earth and the Moon to monitor lunar tides.
explanations: Correct. ISRO identifies the uninterrupted view of the Sun, without occultation or eclipses, as a major advantage of the L1 halo orbit.
L1 is far outside Earth's atmosphere; Aditya-L1 studies the Sun and space weather from a space-based vantage point.
L1 is a gravitational balance region in the rotating Sun–Earth system, not a location with zero gravity or a motionless spacecraft.
Aditya-L1 operates around the Sun–Earth L1 point, not between Earth and the Moon.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology; ISRO, Aditya-L1 mission; https://www.isro.gov.in/Aditya_L1.html

questions.topic: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies
questions.stem: For a plains station that has reached the IMD minimum absolute-temperature condition of at least 40°C, what departure from normal defines a severe heat wave under the departure-based criterion?
options: At least 6.5°C
At least 10°C only when the maximum temperature is 50°C
explanations: This range does not meet the IMD severe category; it is below the departure threshold for a heat wave.
A departure of 4.5°C to 6.4°C meets the heat-wave category, but not the severe heat-wave category.
Correct. For plains stations meeting the minimum absolute-temperature condition, a departure of at least 6.5°C is classified as a severe heat wave.
The IMD does not require a 10°C departure or a 50°C maximum for this departure-based severe category.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies; India Meteorological Department, definition/criteria table, 23 October 2024; https://internal.imd.gov.in/press_release/20241023_pr_3356.pdf

questions.topic: Social Exclusion; Rights issues such as Gender, Caste, Tribe, Disability etc. and inclusive policies
questions.stem: The Constitution (One Hundred and Third Amendment) Act, 2019 inserted which clauses to enable special provisions and reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)?
options: Articles 15(6) and 16(6)
Articles 15(4) and 16(4)
Articles 21A and 45
Articles 243D and 243T
explanations: Correct. The 103rd Amendment inserted Article 15(6) for special provisions including education and Article 16(6) for reservation in public employment for EWS.
Articles 15(4) and 16(4) concern advancement/reservation for socially and educationally backward classes and SC/ST-related provisions, not the EWS clauses inserted by the 103rd Amendment.
Article 21A concerns the right to education for children, while Article 45 is a Directive Principle on early childhood care and education.
Articles 243D and 243T concern reservation in Panchayats and Municipalities, respectively.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Social Exclusion; Rights issues and inclusive policies; Constitution (103rd Amendment) Act, 2019; PIB, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, 9 July 2019; https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1577969

questions.stem: A D flip-flop has an active-low asynchronous reset. The reset is asserted while the clock is stopped. What should happen to the output Q?
options: Q changes only on the next active clock edge.
Q is forced to its reset state without waiting for a clock edge.
Q toggles once because the reset acts as a clock pulse.
Q becomes high-impedance until the clock restarts.
explanations: That describes a synchronous reset, whose effect is sampled at an active clock edge.
Correct. An asserted asynchronous reset acts independently of the clock and forces the flip-flop to its reset state.
A reset is not a clock pulse and does not toggle the stored state.
A reset does not place the flip-flop output in a high-impedance state.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Digital Logic; NPTEL, Digital Electronic Circuits, IIT Kharagpur, counter design with asynchronous reset/preset; https://www.nptel.ac.in/courses/108105132

questions.subtopic: Signed overflow and unsigned wraparound in C
questions.stem: In standard C, an ordinary `int` expression overflows, while an `unsigned int` expression exceeds its maximum. Which statement is correct?
options: Both are defined to wrap modulo the type's range.
Signed overflow is undefined behavior; unsigned arithmetic is reduced modulo one more than its maximum representable value.
Signed overflow saturates at the maximum value; unsigned overflow is undefined.
Both cases must raise a hardware exception.
explanations: Unsigned arithmetic wraps modulo the type's range, but standard signed integer overflow is not defined to wrap.
Correct. A signed result outside the representable range has undefined behavior; unsigned arithmetic is defined modulo one more than the type's maximum value.
C does not generally define signed overflow as saturating, and unsigned overflow is defined rather than undefined.
The C language does not require a hardware exception for either case.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming and Data Structures; ISO/IEC WG14 C11 draft N1570, integer arithmetic rules; SEI CERT C INT32-C; https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1570.pdf ; https://cmu-sei.github.io/secure-coding-standards/sei-cert-c-coding-standard/rules/integers-int/int32-c/

questions.stem: Transaction T1 runs the same predicate query twice. Between the executions, T2 inserts and commits a new row that satisfies the predicate. The new row appears in T1's second result. Which anomaly is illustrated?
options: Dirty read
Non-repeatable read
Phantom read
Lost update
explanations: A dirty read occurs when a transaction reads data written by another transaction before that write is committed; T2 has committed here.
A non-repeatable read changes the value of an existing row that is read again; this scenario changes the set of rows matching a predicate.
Correct. A phantom read occurs when re-executing a predicate query returns a changed set of rows because another transaction committed a matching row.
A lost update occurs when one transaction's write is overwritten by another; no update is lost in this scenario.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; PostgreSQL 18 documentation, Transaction Isolation, SQL-standard definition of phantom read; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/transaction-iso.html

questions.stem: In UML, which rule distinguishes composite aggregation (composition) from shared aggregation?
options: A part may belong to several composite objects at the same time.
The composite is responsible for its parts; a part may belong to at most one composite at a time and is deleted with it if still contained.
Shared aggregation always enforces the same part-lifecycle rule as composition.
Composition differs from association only by the direction of its arrow.
explanations: A part object may be included in at most one composite object at a time, so this statement contradicts composite aggregation.

Correct. UML defines composite aggregation as a strong form in which the composite is responsible for the existence and storage of its parts; a contained part is deleted with the composite unless it is removed first.
The UML specification says the precise semantics of shared aggregation vary by application area and modeler; it does not impose composition's lifecycle rule.
Composition is a form of aggregation with stronger part-ownership/lifecycle semantics, not merely a different arrow direction.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Information Systems and Software Engineering; OMG UML 2.5.1, §9.5.3, AggregationKind semantics; https://www.omg.org/spec/UML/2.5.1/PDF

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.stem: A Java thread calls `obj.wait()` while holding `obj`'s monitor. Which statement correctly describes what happens next?
options: It releases `obj`'s monitor while waiting and must reacquire it before `wait()` returns.
It releases every monitor currently held by the thread.
It immediately transfers the monitor to the thread selected by `notify()`.
It can call `wait()` without owning `obj`'s monitor.
explanations: Correct. `wait()` places the thread in the object's wait set and releases that object's monitor; the thread must reacquire the monitor before it resumes after the wait.
`wait()` releases only the monitor of the object on which it is called; other monitors held by the thread remain held.
`notify()` wakes a waiting thread but does not immediately transfer the monitor; the notifying thread must relinquish it before the awakened thread can reacquire it.
The current thread must own the object's monitor; otherwise `wait()` throws `IllegalMonitorStateException`.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA; Oracle Java SE 8 API, java.lang.Object wait/notify; https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html

questions.stem: A frequent itemset X has no proper superset with the same support count, but some proper superset of X is also frequent with a lower support count. How should X be classified?
options: Closed but not maximal
Maximal but not closed
Neither closed nor frequent
Both maximal and closed
explanations: Correct. X is closed because no proper superset has the same support; it is not maximal because at least one proper superset is still frequent.
A maximal frequent itemset has no frequent proper superset, which is not true in this scenario.
X is explicitly frequent and satisfies the definition of closed, so this option is false.
The frequent proper superset means X is not maximal, even though it is closed.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; LMU Munich, Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining 1, frequent-pattern mining lecture notes, pp. 161–162; Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques, 3rd ed.; https://www.dbs.ifi.lmu.de/Lehre/KDD/WS1920/lecture_notes/KDD1_IV_III_1.pdf
